Everything that *supports* the lectures lives on this page: longer written references (appendices) you can read at your own pace, a glossary, cheat sheets, UO computing services, free books and tutorials, and key papers on reproducible computational research. The lectures cover each topic briefly; the appendices go deeper.

## Course reference material

Read these **on demand** - when a lecture moves too fast, when you're doing homework, or when you need to look something up.

| Appendix | Topic | Goes with |
|:--:|---|:--:|
| [Glossary](Resources_Folder/Glossary.qmd) | Definitions of the computing terms used in this course - keep it open during lectures | All |
| [A](Resources_Folder/Appendix_A_Computer_Systems_Command_Line.qmd) | **Computer Systems & the Command Line** - hardware, operating systems, getting a shell (including WSL on Windows), VS Code/Positron, paths, files, wildcards, pipes, `wget`/`curl` | Lectures 00 - 04 |
| [B](Resources_Folder/Appendix_B_GREP_Regex_Shell.qmd) | **GREP, Regular Expressions & Shell Scripting** - `grep`, regex syntax, `sed`, `awk`, variables, loops, functions, error handling | Lectures 05 - 06 |
| [C](Resources_Folder/Appendix_C_Git_GitHub.qmd) | **Git, GitHub & Version Control** - commits, remotes, branches, authentication, `.gitignore`, GitHub Pages | Lectures 08 - 09 |
| [D](Resources_Folder/Appendix_D_R_and_RStudio.qmd) | **R Primer** - RStudio, Positron, vectors, data frames, factors, functions, packages, dplyr, ggplot2 | Lecture 07 |
| [E](Resources_Folder/Appendix_E_Core_R_Commands.qmd) | **Core R Commands Reference** - a task-organized look-up for everyday R | Lecture 07 onward |
| [F](Resources_Folder/Appendix_F_Quarto_Markdown.qmd) | **Quarto & Markdown Syntax** - YAML, code chunks and options, figures, tables, callouts, math, citations, rendering | Lectures 00, 08 |
| [G](Resources_Folder/Appendix_G_Data_Formats_Repositories.qmd) | **Common Data Formats & Public Repositories** - CSV/TSV, FASTA, FASTQ, GFF, BED, VCF, HDF5; NCBI, EBI, Ensembl, Zenodo; FAIR data | Lectures 03 - 05 |

## UO computing resources

-   [UO Service Portal](https://service.uoregon.edu) - knowledge base and help tickets for all UO technology
-   [Duck ID account management](https://duckid.uoregon.edu) - passwords and two-step login (Duo)
-   [UO Software Downloads](https://software.uoregon.edu) - site-licensed software (MATLAB, Mathematica, LabVIEW, SPSS, ArcGIS, ...) - log in with your Duck ID
-   [Microsoft 365 at UO](https://office.uoregon.edu) - Outlook, Teams, OneDrive (1 TB), Office apps
-   [Getting started with OneDrive](https://service.uoregon.edu/TDClient/2030/Portal/KB/ArticleDet?ID=33095) · [UO Dropbox FAQ](https://service.uoregon.edu/TDClient/2030/Portal/KB/ArticleDet?ID=102573)
-   [UO VPN](https://service.uoregon.edu/TDClient/2030/Portal/KB/ArticleDet?ID=31471) - for campus-restricted resources when off campus
-   [UO AI service offerings](https://service.uoregon.edu/TDClient/2030/Portal/KB/Article/140911/AI-Service-Offerings) - supported AI tools and which data classifications they allow
-   [Talapas Knowledge Base](https://uoracs.github.io/talapas2-knowledge-base/) - UO's HPC cluster (Research Advanced Computing Services, racs\@uoregon.edu)
-   [UO Libraries - Research Data Management](https://researchguides.uoregon.edu/data-management) - data management plans, storage, and sharing

## Free books and tutorials

**The command line**

-   [Software Carpentry - The Unix Shell](https://swcarpentry.github.io/shell-novice/) - the classic hands-on introduction
-   [The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT)](https://missing.csail.mit.edu/) - shell, scripting, editors, Git, and more
-   Buffalo, V. (2015). [*Bioinformatics Data Skills*](https://vincebuffalo.com/book/). O'Reilly - command-line data skills for biologists

**R and Python**

-   Wickham, Çetinkaya-Rundel & Grolemund. [*R for Data Science* (2e)](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) - the standard free book for modern R
-   Wickham et al. [*ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis*](https://ggplot2-book.org/)
-   Wickham. [*Advanced R*](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/) - for when you want to know how R really works
-   [Software Carpentry - Programming with R](https://swcarpentry.github.io/r-novice-inflammation/) and [Programming with Python](https://swcarpentry.github.io/python-novice-inflammation/)
-   VanderPlas. [*Python Data Science Handbook*](https://jakevdp.github.io/PythonDataScienceHandbook/)

**Reproducibility, Git, and Quarto**

-   Chacon & Straub. [*Pro Git*](https://git-scm.com/book) - everything about Git, free online
-   Bryan. [*Happy Git and GitHub for the useR*](https://happygitwithr.com/) - Git for R users
-   [Software Carpentry - Version Control with Git](https://swcarpentry.github.io/git-novice/)
-   [GitHub Skills](https://skills.github.com/) - short interactive GitHub courses
-   [Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/guide/) and [Publishing to GitHub Pages](https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html)
-   [The Turing Way](https://book.the-turing-way.org/) - a community handbook for reproducible, ethical data science

## Key papers on computational practice

Short, readable papers worth your time early in grad school:

-   Wilson, G. et al. (2014). Best practices for scientific computing. *PLoS Biology* 12: e1001745. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.1001745>
-   Wilson, G. et al. (2017). Good enough practices in scientific computing. *PLoS Computational Biology* 13: e1005510. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005510>
-   Noble, W. S. (2009). A quick guide to organizing computational biology projects. *PLoS Computational Biology* 5: e1000424. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1000424>
-   Sandve, G. K. et al. (2013). Ten simple rules for reproducible computational research. *PLoS Computational Biology* 9: e1003285. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285>
-   Wickham, H. (2014). Tidy data. *Journal of Statistical Software* 59(10). <https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v059.i10>
-   Broman, K. W. & Woo, K. H. (2018). Data organization in spreadsheets. *The American Statistician* 72: 2-10. <https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2017.1375989>
-   Ziemann, M., Eren, Y. & El-Osta, A. (2016). Gene name errors are widespread in the scientific literature. *Genome Biology* 17: 177. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-1044-7>
-   Blischak, J. D., Davenport, E. R. & Wilson, G. (2016). A quick introduction to version control with Git and GitHub. *PLoS Computational Biology* 12: e1004668. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004668>
-   Perez-Riverol, Y. et al. (2016). Ten simple rules for taking advantage of Git and GitHub. *PLoS Computational Biology* 12: e1004947. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004947>
-   Wilkinson, M. D. et al. (2016). The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship. *Scientific Data* 3: 160018. <https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18>

## Public data repositories

A short list - see [Appendix G](Resources_Folder/Appendix_G_Data_Formats_Repositories.qmd) for what each holds and how to choose.

-   [NCBI](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) - [GEO](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/) (expression data), [SRA](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sra) (raw reads), [GenBank](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genbank/) (sequences)
-   [EMBL-EBI / ENA](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/home) - the European mirror of sequence archives
-   [Ensembl](https://www.ensembl.org/) and [UCSC Genome Browser](https://genome.ucsc.edu/) - reference genomes and annotations
-   [Protein Data Bank (RCSB PDB)](https://www.rcsb.org/) - 3D structures of proteins and nucleic acids
-   [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/), [Dryad](https://datadryad.org/), and [Figshare](https://figshare.com/) - general-purpose data archives with DOIs

## Getting help

-   **Ask early.** Office hours are Tuesday 3:00 - 4:00 in the KC Connector - or email to set up a time.
-   **Read the error message** - then paste it into a search engine (or a UO-supported AI assistant, using only green data).
-   Built-in help: `man command` in the shell, `?function` in R, `help(function)` in Python.
-   [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/) and [Posit Community](https://forum.posit.co/) - most questions have already been asked and answered.
